Hi Julia — thanks for the context and the diagram. Looping in Rishi (legal) and Marissa (sales) so we can align on acceptable contract language and the commercial tradeoffs.

Quick notes:
- We generally don’t agree to unlimited exposure without mitigation (escrow / insurance / narrower scope).
- Typical options we offer: (1) carve-out limited to direct damages arising from proven third-party IP infringement where Customer provides timely notice and control of defense; (2) carve-out but with a cap equal to the order value or a multiple; (3) keep cap but allow for separate escrow or enhanced insurance proof as a condition.

Rishi — can you propose preferred language and a fallback? Marissa — heads up on possible pricing/term implications if Acme insists on a broad carve-out.

Hannah

On Mon, Nov 1, 2027 at 9:12 AM Julia Park <julia.park@acme.com> wrote:
> Hi Hannah,
> 
> Quick question as we're reviewing the latest order form: our legal team is pushing for an explicit carve-out to the liability cap for IP indemnity (they want IP claims to sit outside the cap entirely)...

Proposed approach from Redwood legal: two-tiered path to balance Acme's concern and Redwood's exposure.

1) Narrow the carve-out scope. Language we prefer:
   - "Notwithstanding the foregoing, claims finally judicially determined to constitute third-party intellectual property infringement shall not be subject to the limitation of liability set forth in Section [X], provided that Customer (a) gives Provider prompt written notice of any such claim, (b) cooperates with Provider in the defense, and (c) assigns to Provider any rights Customer may have against its customer to pursue a recovery."

2) Mitigate exposure via operational guardrails: require Customer to provide (i) evidence of ownership or license (reasonable documentation), and (ii) either: a) an insurance certificate evidencing commercial general liability or cyber/tech E&O coverage with an IP endorsement (limits to be discussed), or b) willingness to fund an escrow for source/verification in the narrow circumstances where Provider can show no available mitigation.

3) Commercial fallback if Acme insists on an unconditional carve-out: increase the liability cap for IP claims to a defined multiple of the annual fees (e.g., 2x annual fees) and include a carve-out only for direct damages (no consequential).

I am attaching a proposed redline snippet for the MSA / order form. If Acme will accept proof-of-rights + insurance certificate, we can keep the standard cap and avoid price increases. If they require an unconditional outside-the-cap carve-out, Sales should expect a pricing uplift and we will require exec legal sign-off.

Attachment: proposed_redline.docx

-Rishi
